answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can use a shared staking pool called the meadow, where each new identity must deposit a minimum onyx-rated bond of locked capital. Attackers face high cost because fabricating many identities requires multiplying the locked funds, and any detected duplicate triggers a raven-like swift slashing that burns the bond, making large-scale attacks economically unviable as the attacker cost scales linearly with the number of sybils while rewards do not.
